doc.title: Dave Liebman — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Terumasa Hino's Journey to Air session
summary: Kirchner reads the personnel of Hino's 1970 New York session, which Liebman likens to Ascension.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Next is your first recording that you made for Japan, but in New York, with Terumasa Hino, by 1970, Journey to Air.
That’s one of – that’s Hino getting – that’s Ascension. That’s Hino with whomever. Do they have the list of characters?
Olu Dara, Pete Yellin, Gary Pribec, Grossman, Mike Garson, Lanny Fields, Dave Holland, Teruo Nakamura, Moses, and Motohiko Hino.

Okay. We’re all in the studio together. I think the whole thing is Ascension. That’s a free – because Hino would come over and do something with American musicians. Upsurge Studios, 55 West 19th Street, Tom Di Pietro.
